GPS anti-spoofing protects an authorized military ranging service by encrypting the precise code so that an adversary cannot easily imitate it. A receiver without the required keys cannot reproduce and authenticate the protected sequence in the same way. Anti-spoofing addresses acceptance of false signals, whereas [[Selective Availability]] reduced the accuracy of the open service; the two mechanisms therefore pursued different security goals.

GPS aviation navigation replaces dependence on a chain of nearby ground beacons with global three-dimensional position and route guidance. Aviation adoption required more than raw accuracy: users needed integrity, rapid warning of faulty data, dependable coverage, and adequate vertical performance for approach operations. Augmentation systems compare GPS against surveyed ground sites and broadcast corrections and status, allowing smaller airports to gain guidance without installing a complete local precision-approach system.

GPS fleet and asset tracking couples a passive navigation receiver to a communication link that reports position, speed, or events to another party. Dispatchers can coordinate vehicles and emergency services can locate crashes, but the same capability enables employers or service providers to monitor individuals. The tracking function is therefore not performed by GPS alone: GPS supplies location, while a cellular or radio transmitter converts that private local estimate into remotely observable data.

GPS full operational capability marked the transition from a developing constellation to a service able to meet its specified worldwide military mission. Achieving it required enough operational satellites and spares, a mature ground-control network, production receivers, and validated performance rather than merely a successful prototype. The declaration in the mid-1990s also created a stable platform for rapidly expanding civil and commercial reliance.

GPS III M-code is a modern protected military signal designed to improve resistance to jamming and hostile manipulation. Additional signal power and coding capabilities help authorized receivers acquire and track navigation data in contested environments, while separation from civil signals supports selective military operation. M-code strengthens one layer of GPS but does not remove the need for redundant satellites, ground control, inertial integration, and interference awareness.

GPS jamming overwhelms the weak satellite signal at a receiver with stronger radio energy in or near the navigation band. Spread-spectrum correlation provides processing gain, but the signals arrive below the ordinary noise floor after traveling from medium Earth orbit, so a nearby low-cost transmitter can deny service over a useful area. Detection, adaptive filtering, protected signals, directional antennas, and independent navigation methods reduce the effect without eliminating the underlying power imbalance.

GPS Phase I was the concept-validation period in which experimental transmitters, satellites, and receivers tested whether the proposed architecture worked as a system. Ground-based pseudo-satellites at New Mexico test ranges exercised code ranging before launch, and the NTS and early Block I satellites validated spaceborne clocks, signals, and user equipment. Validation reduced the risk of committing to a full global constellation while revealing receiver and signal problems that required redesign.

GPS precision agriculture uses repeatable position to coordinate field operations with spatial data. Corrected receivers can guide tractors along closely spaced passes, reduce overlap, and associate soil, yield, fertilizer, or pesticide information with particular parts of a field. The value comes from returning machinery and measurements to the same coordinate framework, so improved relative accuracy and dependable availability often matter more than a consumer receiver's standalone location display.

GPS spoofing presents counterfeit navigation signals that cause a receiver to compute a plausible but false position or time. It is more deceptive than jamming because the receiver may continue reporting a solution. Differential services address integrity with monitoring, error-detecting codes, and central alerts, while protected military codes add authentication. Cross-checking other constellations, inertial behavior, maps, clocks, or independent sensors helps expose inconsistencies.

GPS timing infrastructure uses the constellation's disciplined time scale as a common reference for distributed systems. A stationary receiver that already knows its location can focus on clock synchronization rather than navigation, delivering precise timing to telecommunications and other networks. This role is largely invisible to end users but makes loss or corruption of satellite signals an infrastructure problem even where no one is actively viewing a map.

Multiple What Now?
Chrome is a multithreaded browser—it uses different threads for different dedicated
tasks. This enables different kinds of work to be done in parallel—without blocking
progress. Rasterization, the process of converting vector shapes to raster format (pix‐
els) to be displayed onto a screen, is done on a dedicated rasterization thread. At
times, Chrome may decide the device being used is best served by running multiple
rasterization threads in parallel—greatly speeding up the process of getting pixels
onto your screen. If it’s able to do this, Chrome won’t use the GPU for decoding.
While you, the developer, have control over ensuring the proper meta viewport ele‐
ment is being used, you have no control over whether or not there are multiple raster‐
ization threads. So, while you can provide Chrome what it needs to handle decoding
on the GPU, ultimately it’s the browser that decides if it should happen or not.
Summary
The browser has to do a lot of work to display an image on your screen. Sizing your
images appropriately, taking advantage of chroma subsampling on your JPEG files,
and taking advantage of GPU decoding can all help to reduce the impact on both
processing and memory—both very important considerations particularly on mobile

GPU partitioning (GPU-P) is a new feature for the Hyper-V role in Windows Server 2025, which allows
you to share a physical GPU across multiple VMs. When utilizing GPU-P, your VMs can each receive a
dedicated fraction of the GPU, not a simple pass-through of hardware to the VM. This may sound similar
to functionality that already existed, previously provided by Discrete Device Assignment (DDA), but
there are some key differences. The older DDA can intentionally allocate dedicated GPU resources to
VMs, but on a 1:1 ratio. DDA can assign an entire GPU to a VM. GPU-P, on the other hand, allows you
to chop up those massive GPU cards and assign segments (fractions) of them to VMs, allowing you to
utilize large GPUs and spread that processing load across many servers.
GPU-P is going to be useful for VDI-type environments, especially where you need high rendering
capacity. DDA is cool, but it requires many physical GPUs if you need multiple high-powered VMs.
GPU-P widens this bottleneck, allowing you to do more with less physical hardware. Keep in mind
that you cannot share GPUs via both DDA and GPU-P at the same time!

Graph feature extraction manually derives variables from known graph statistics, motifs, paths, or domain-specific relationships. It exposes interpretable structural hypotheses to a conventional learning model.

Its strength is control over what each dimension means. Its limitation is dependence on prior knowledge and the cost of designing features that transfer across network types and tasks.

Graph feature generation converts nodes, edges, neighborhoods, or whole networks into numerical representations. Features may be designed from known structural measures or learned as embeddings from graph relationships.

The representation scale must match the prediction target. Local features describe a node's immediate context, global features encode broader position, and learned vectors can combine multiple structural regularities.

Graph path length measures the total cost of a [[Graph Path]]. In an unweighted graph it can be counted as the number of edges. In a [[Weighted Graph]], it is the sum of the weights assigned to the traversed edges.

The meaning of a weight comes from the model. It may represent physical distance, travel time, cost, reward, or another quantity, so the shortest path is defined relative to that chosen measure.

Graph relaxation improves a provisional estimate when a newly examined route is better. A shortest-path algorithm may begin with deliberately extreme estimates—zero for the starting vertex and infinity elsewhere—and replace them with progressively smaller distances.

In [[Dijkstra's Algorithm]], examining an edge from the current vertex asks whether the known distance to that vertex plus the edge weight beats the neighbor's current estimate. If so, both the distance and predecessor are updated.

Graph transduction predicts labels for the particular unlabeled nodes already present in a similarity graph. It seeks an assignment consistent with known labels and strong connections rather than learning only a general function for future cases.

Because the test nodes participate directly in the optimization, transductive predictions can exploit their joint geometry. New observations usually require rebuilding or extending the graph instead of applying a fixed inductive rule.

GRAPHICS DEBUGGERS
One difficulty with writing increasingly complex graphics code is that it is more difficult
to debug than normal C++ code. With C++ code, if there is an issue, you can place a
breakpoint and step through the execution of the code. However, if the game does not
show the correct graphics output, it could be one of several issues. It might be that you’re
calling the wrong OpenGL functions, or the data passed to the shaders is wrong, or the
GLSL shader code is wrong.
This difficulty in determining the source of problems led to the creation of graphics
debuggers. There are several graphics debuggers available, some of which are proprietary
to specific types of graphics hardware or consoles. At a minimum, these debuggers allow
you to capture a frame of graphics data and step through the commands executed to see
how the output to the framebuffer changes. They also allow you to view all the data sent
to the GPU, including vertex data, textures, and shader constants. Some even allow you to
step through the execution of a vertex or pixel shader to see where it goes wrong.
For Windows and Linux, the best graphics debugger that supports OpenGL is RenderDoc
(https://renderdoc.org), an open source tool created by Baldur Karlsson. In addition to
OpenGL, it supports debugging for Vulkan as well as Microsoft Direct3D 11 and 12 (the latter
two only on Windows). Unfortunately, at this writing, RenderDoc has no macOS support.
For macOS users, Intel Graphics Performance Analyzers (GPA) is a great alternative. See
https://software.intel.com/en-us/gpa.

Domain applications show why no infrastructure is useful without a meaningful data lifecycle. [[Genomic Big Data Analysis]] begins with high-throughput sequencing and follows genomic records through acquisition, transfer, storage, and analysis. Precision medicine relates molecular variation to an individual's likely response, while cancer genomics investigates mutations and pathways across tumors. Public projects such as ENCODE and the Cancer Genomics Hub illustrate the scientific value and operational burden of shared data. Formats, metadata, bandwidth, privacy, provenance, and reproducible workflows must develop together.

Technical feasibility is still not financial justification. [[Big Data Project Value Management]] treats an initiative as a portfolio of interdependent subprojects whose order changes cash flows. Net present value discounts future benefits and costs; incremental funding can test or deliver useful components before the whole portfolio is complete. Dependency constraints rule out some sequences, and limited capital may make it rational to omit a subproject. Project selection should therefore compare feasible funding sequences, opportunity costs, and risk rather than assuming that every technically attractive component must be built.

[[Hospital Big Data Analytics]] turns historical treatment records into operational predictions. Large, high-dimensional, noisy data must be cleaned before a parallel random forest can model how long a patient's treatment task may take. Predicted task durations and current queues support route recommendations intended to reduce waiting and overcrowding. This is an operations problem as much as a modeling problem: timestamps, patient attributes, dependencies among examinations, queue updates, and deployment constraints determine whether a prediction improves actual flow. Intelligent triage must also remain accountable to clinical priorities that the scheduling model does not replace.

Finally, [[Vehicular Cloud Computing]] asks whether the underused processors, storage, sensors, and communication devices in parked vehicles can form a data center. Ephemeral vehicular clouds are poorly suited to long computations because vehicles leave before virtual machines can be prepared or migrated. Long-term parking creates more stable residence times, and a high-bandwidth wired fabric avoids the bottleneck of many wireless designs. Data replication and virtual-machine migration preserve work as membership changes. The proposal connects resource sharing, incentives, topology, reliability, and conventional cloud economics in an unusual physical platform.

Gravitational field strength is force per unit test mass, $g=F/m$. Around a spherical mass $M$, its magnitude is $GM/r^2$ and its direction is inward. It is also the local acceleration of freely falling matter when other forces are negligible, giving it equivalent units of $\mathrm{N\,kg^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

Gravitational potential is gravitational potential energy per unit mass. Taking zero at infinity, the potential outside a spherical mass is $\phi=-GM/r$. Potential is scalar and adds algebraically for multiple masses. Gravitational field points toward decreasing potential, and moving a mass through a potential difference changes its potential energy by $m\Delta\phi$.

Gravitational time dilation means that clocks deeper in a gravitational field run more slowly than clocks at higher gravitational potential. The effect follows from curved spacetime and is distinct from motion-based [[Time Dilation]]. Satellite navigation must correct for both effects to preserve timing and position accuracy.

Grease Pencil appearance comes from object materials rather than being stored only in the drawing brush. Material slots act like a palette of defined stroke and fill treatments.

Its layers form an ordered stack in which higher layers can cover lower ones. Layers can be tinted, assigned pass indices or view layers, and controlled separately, joining familiar drawing organization with Blender's rendering and compositing structure.

Grease Pencil modifiers apply broad procedural changes to a drawing without editing every stroke point. Like mesh modifiers, they are managed in the modifier stack and remain adjustable until applied.

Layer and material controls can restrict where a modifier acts. Modifiers can automate visual effects and also support rigs that animate a drawing through controls rather than requiring every frame to be redrawn.

Grease Pencil stores drawn strokes as editable objects in three-dimensional space. A 2D Animation start file presents a light canvas-like Viewport through the scene camera while retaining access to Blender's 3D tools.

Strokes have control points that can be sculpted or edited and can move nearer to or farther from the camera. This makes Grease Pencil suitable for both flat animation and 2.5D drawings integrated with a 3D scene.

Grease Pencil is also a first-class Blender object type, so drawings can be positioned and organized beside meshes, curves, lights, and cameras. This object-level status lets drawn elements participate in the same scene hierarchy as the environment they annotate or depict.

Grease Pencil supports a traditional hand-drawn workflow and a rigged workflow closer to 3D character animation. Hand-drawn work creates and refines new stroke states over time; rigging reuses controls and deformations.

The choice depends on the desired visual style and production method. Both approaches retain access to Blender's camera, timeline, materials, compositing, and three-dimensional scene, so they can also be combined.

Greedy best-first search expands the frontier node with the smallest heuristic estimate to the goal. It follows apparently promising directions without including the path cost already accumulated.

Greedy layer-wise pretraining trains one [[Autoencoder|encoder]] on raw inputs, keeps its encoding layer, and then trains another encoder to reconstruct that first layer's representation. Repeating this builds a stack of representations before the final prediction task is fitted.

Each layer is optimized for its own reconstruction task rather than the eventual output, which is why the process is called greedy. A later tuning phase can freeze the pretrained layers or adjust the whole network using target labels. Grid alignment controls items within their grid areas and the track collection within the grid container. `justify-*` properties operate on the inline axis, while `align-*` properties operate on the block axis; item and content variants select the subject being aligned.

Grid items can occupy the same cells and overlap. Document order and `z-index` then determine their painting layers according to [[CSS Stacking Order]].

Grid auto-placement assigns positions to items whose row, column, or both axes remain automatic. The algorithm moves through the grid by row or column and creates [[CSS Implicit Grid|implicit tracks]] as needed.

A dense mode can backfill earlier holes with later items that fit, but this can make visual order differ from source order. Explicitly positioned items reserve their occupied cells before the remaining items are placed.

Grid gaps are spaces inserted between adjacent row or column tracks. In the source's property names, `grid-row-gap`, `grid-column-gap`, and `grid-gap` define nonnegative lengths or percentages for the two axes.

Gaps consume space during [[CSS Grid Track Sizing]] as if the separating grid lines had thickness. Content-distribution alignment can add further spacing, but the declared gap itself remains distinct from margins on individual items.

Grid lines divide a grid into row and column tracks. The intersection of one row track and one column track is a cell, while a grid area is a rectangular collection of one or more cells.

Lines can be numbered or named, and areas can receive names through the grid template. Placement addresses the bounding lines or an area name rather than inserting content into a separate table-like structure.

Grid track sizing defines the widths of columns and heights of rows. Tracks can use fixed or percentage lengths, content-based keywords, flexible fractions, and functions such as `minmax()` that place lower and upper bounds on growth.

Intrinsic content can expand a track when the sizing function permits it. Gaps and fixed tracks consume space before [[CSS Fractional Grid Units]] divide the remaining amount.

Next, we come to the ListView. The key to understanding XAML is composition: you can
achieve almost any effect because you can place a control inside another control. In the case
of a ListView control, you essentially have two elements of the control: the data that it's
displaying and how it displays that data.
<ListView Grid.Row="0" ItemsSource="{Binding ChatHistory}">
We'll come back to exactly what ChatHistory is later, but for now, just think of it as a
collection. We're binding the ItemSource — that is, the data source of the control — to the
collection of things, called ChatHistory. That's the what; the next part is how:
<ListView.ItemTemplate>
<DataTemplate x:DataType="models:ChatMessage">
<StackPanel Orientation="Horizontal">
<TextBlock Text="{Binding Sender}"/>
<TextBlock Text=":"/>
<TextBlock Text="{Binding Message}"/>
</StackPanel>
</DataTemplate>

Here, we're using DataTemplate to tell the ListView that each element will be of the
ChatMessage type; again, we'll come back to what that is — the important thing is that it

declaring a StackPanel, and inside of that, we're declaring a number of TextBlock
elements. This is what I mean by composition — if you want to display a list of elements in a
list, then you need to define where that data is and exactly how to display it.
While this process is more verbose than other technologies, it affords a
much greater degree of flexibility — for example, you could have an image

Griefing is intentional harassment of another player or community outside the accepted social norms of an online game. It ranges from disruptive annoyance to threats or abuse with serious real-world consequences.

Mechanics, reporting, moderation, identity controls, and community standards all affect its cost and visibility. A technically permitted action can still be griefing when its purpose is to prevent others from participating.

Grinding is the repetition of already mastered actions for the sake of accumulating rewards or resources. Its main demand is usually time, patience, and endurance rather than deeper understanding of the game's rules.

Grinding can let a player trade time for reduced future difficulty, such as by increasing an avatar's numerical power. It can also become filler that disrespects the player's time when prolonged repetition is required mainly to delay progress or sustain engagement.

GROOVE WELD STRENGTH
There are two basic types of groove welds: complete joint penetration (CJP) welds and partial
joint penetration (PJP) welds (see Figure 10-16 for groove welds). The strength of a joint made
with a CJP weld is a function of the strength of the base metal because the CJP weld completely
fuses the two connecting parts together as if they were one member. For a CJP weld in tension,
the nominal strength would be the product of the cross-sectional area of the smaller of the steel
elements being joined and the yield strength of the steel. The process of making a CJP weld
requires providing weld metal throughout the entire depth of the joint. The best quality CJP
weld is one in which the weld metal is applied to one side through the entire base metal thick -
ness and then the opposite side is backgouged, or cleaned and prepared for the application of
more weld metal (see Figure 10-16a). An alternate way to place the weld metal is to provide a

Running a Formal Individual Playtest
Investigators should seek to make the individual playtest as similar as possible to the
experience that a player who bought the game would have at home. The playtester
should be comfortable and at ease. You might want to provide snacks or drinks, and
if the game is designed for tablet or console, you might want to give them a couch or
other comfortable seat to sit on. (For computer games, a desk and office chair are often
more appropriate.)

Start the playtest by telling the playtester how much you appreciate the time they have
set aside to test your game and how useful it will be for you to get their feedback. You
should also request that they please speak their thoughts out loud while playing. Few
playtesters will actually do so, but it can't hurt to ask.
After the playtester has finished the section of the game that you want them to play, an
investigator should sit with the playtester and discuss their experience with the game.
The questions asked by the investigator should be similar to those that are asked at the
end of formal group testing, but the one-on-one format will allow the investigator to
frame meaningful follow-up questions and get better information. The post-playtest
question and answer sessions should also be recorded, though audio recording is more
important than video for the post-play interview.
As with all formal playtesting, it is best if the investigator is not part of the game devel-
opment team. This helps the investigator's questions and perceptions to not be biased
by personal investment in the game. However, when you have found a good investiga-
tor, it is very useful to work with the same investigator throughout the development
process so that they can provide you information about the progression of playtesters'
reactions to the game over the course of development.

Problem: You want to use a non-parametric test to compare if two
independent groups of sampled data have equally large values.
Solution: The Mann–Whitney U test (also called the Mann–Whitney–
Wilcoxon or Wilcoxon rank-sum test) is a non-parametric test that is
used to compare the location shift between two independent groups of
ordinal or quantitative data. The test can be employed when the nor-
mality assumption of a two-sample t -test is not met.
The function wilcox.test calculates the Mann–Whitney U test
statistic and tests the hypothesis that the difference in location between
the two groups is zero. Input to wilcox.test can either be a formula
or two vectors representing the values from the two groups.
In the example below we use the ToothGrowth data to examine if the
supplement type (orange juice or ascorbic acid) of vitamin C influences
the length of teeth in guinea pigs.
> data(ToothGrowth)

Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction

W = 600, p-value = 0.06
alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0
We obtain a test statistic of 575.5 which yields a p -value of 0.06449.

Host attestations
Attestation of the guarded hosts is the secret to using shielded VMs. This is the basis of security in
wanting to move forward with such a solution in your own environment. The ability of your hosts
to attest their health and identity gives you peace of mind in knowing that those hosts are not being
modified or manipulated without your knowledge, and it ensures that a malicious host employee
cannot copy all of your VM hard drive files onto a USB, bring them home, and boot them up. Those
shielded VMs are only ever going to start on the guarded hosts in your environment, nowhere else.
There are two different modes that guarded hosts can use to pass attestation with HGS. Well, actually,
there are three, but one has already been deprecated. Let’s take a minute to detail the different modes
that can be used between your guarded hosts and your HGS.
TPM-trusted attestations
This is the best way! TPM chips are physical chips installed on your server’s motherboard that contain
unique information. Most importantly, this information cannot be modified or hacked from within
the Windows operating system. When your guarded host servers are equipped with TPM 2.0 chips,
this opens the door to doing some incredibly powerful host attestation. The host utilizes Secure Boot
and some code integrity checks that are stored inside the TPM to verify that it is healthy and has
not been modified. HGS then cross-checks the information being submitted from the TPM with the
information that it knows about when the guarded host was initially configured, to ensure that the
requesting host is really one of your approved guarded hosts and that it has not been tampered with.
If you are configuring new Hyper-V servers, make sure they contain TPM 2.0 chips so that you can
utilize these features.
Host key attestations
If TPMs aren’t your thing or are beyond your hardware abilities, we can do a simpler host key attestation.
The ability of your guarded hosts to generate a host key that can be known and verified by HGS is new
as of Windows Server 2019. This uses asymmetric key-pair technology to validate the guarded hosts.
Basically, you will either create a new host-key pair or use an existing certificate, and then send the
public portion of that key or certificate over to HGS. When guarded hosts want to spin up a shielded
VM, they reach out to attest with HGS, and that attestation is approved or denied based on this key pair.

From the kernel documentation: “The overcommit amount can be set via vm.overcommit_ratio (percentage)

With the vm.overcommit_memory tunable set to 0, the default, there is no formula to calculate the total

• It runs out of Virtual Address Space (VAS); on older 32-bit systems, this is a distinct possibility,
very much less so on 64-bit (the one we’re typically running upon, as the VAS is vast there).
• It truly exhausts all memory (in the entire hierarchy, the memory pyramid) – CPU caches,
RAM, and swap are all used up; in spite of efforts to reclaim memory frames, this can fail in
the face of enormous memory pressure (as is indeed going to be applied here!). Now there’s
no choice: the kernel invokes the OOM killer.
